ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy early set with standout Morning Dew and Viola Lee Blues
ai_show_review.blurb: The three‑song set opens with a powerful rendition of Morning Dew, moves into an expansive jam on Viola Lee Blues, and closes with the vocal‑driven Good Morning Little Schoolgirl. The soundboard source provides good fidelity and maintains high energy throughout.
ai_show_review.review: On January 14, 1967 at San Francisco’s Fillmore Auditorium, a youthful Grateful Dead delivered a concise three‑song set that already hinted at the exploratory spirit they would become famous for. Jerry’s plaintive lead on Morning Dew sets an urgent tone, while Phil and Bob lock into a deep groove that fuels Pigpen’s gritty organ swells during Viola Lee Blues – a jam that feels both raw and inspired. The evening wraps with Good Morning Little Schoolgirl, where Bob’s rhythm guitar and the band’s vocal harmonies take center stage, showcasing their early blues‑rock sensibility. Though only three numbers are captured, the soundboard recording preserves enough clarity to hear each instrument’s character, making this a valuable snapshot of the Dead in their formative months.

best_recording.reason: Good‑quality soundboard capture that faithfully renders the early three‑song set with clear instrument separation and high energy.

key_highlights: Powerful opening with Morning Dew showcasing early emotive guitar work
Jam‑heavy Viola Lee Blues featuring expansive organ textures and tight rhythm section
Vocal‑centric Good Morning Little Schoolgirl that highlights the band's blues roots
Soundboard recording offers clear fidelity for this formative performance
